simulator_description: This simulator models a single-stage Beer Game supply chain over discrete time, where the state tracks on-hand inventory, unmet demand as backlog, and a shipment pipeline represented as (quantity, remaining lead time) tuples. At each step it updates the system by (i) advancing the pipeline and adding any arrivals to inventory, (ii) sampling exogenous customer demand using an overdispersed Gamma-Poisson (negative-binomial-like) process with mild seasonality, and (iii) placing the agent’s provided order into the pipeline with a stochastic lead time drawn from a categorical distribution over 1–5 periods; three alternative within-step update conventions (arrivals/demand/order orderings) are selectable via learned logits. The accounting is conservative and standard for inventory/backlog systems—fulfillment ships up to available inventory against backlog plus new demand—while using the action directly as the order quantity (action-first) ensures trajectories reflect the external policy, and parsing true pipeline tuples (or using zero-quantity dummies when only length is known) avoids fabricating supply that would distort dynamics.
